title.zh: 卷二十一 列傳第十一 王弘
title.raw: 卷二十一 列傳第十一 王弘 Volume 21 Biographies 11: Wang Hong

sentences.zh: 王弘，字休元，琅邪临沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Hong, styled Xiuyuan, was a man of Langya Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hong, courtesy name Xiuyuan, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.

sentences.zh: 曾祖导，晋丞相，祖洽，中领军，父珣，司徒。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dao was Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia was Central Army Commander; his father Xun was Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dao had served as Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia as Central Army Commander; his father Xun as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 弘少好學，以清悟知名。

translations.literal: Hong from youth loved learning and was famed for lucid insight.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Hong loved study and won renown for clear, penetrating mind.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為會稽王道子驃騎主簿。

translations.literal: At weak-crown age he became chief clerk to Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, in the office of the Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he served as chief clerk to Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, under the Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 珣頗好積聚，財物布在人間，及薨，弘悉燔券書，一不收責，其餘舊業，悉委諸弟。

translations.literal: Xun greatly loved accumulation; wealth and goods were spread among the people, and when he died Hong burned all bond-deeds and collected nothing owed; the rest of the old estate he wholly entrusted to his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had been fond of amassing wealth, with loans scattered far and wide; when he died Hong burned every bond and pressed no debtor for repayment, turning the remainder of the family holdings over entirely to his younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 時內外多難，在喪者皆不得終其哀，唯弘徵召一無所就。

translations.literal: At the time troubles were many within and without; those in mourning could not complete their grief, yet Hong alone accepted no summons whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was racked by turmoil inside and out, and mourners could scarcely finish their rites—yet Hong alone refused every summons that reached him.

sentences.zh: 桓玄克建業，收道子付廷尉，臣吏莫敢瞻送，弘時尚居喪，獨道側拜辭，攀車涕泣，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan took Jianye he handed Daozi over to the Court of Justice; no clerk or officer dared look on or escort him; Hong was still in mourning yet alone bowed and took leave by the roadside, clinging to the carriage and weeping; commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized Jianye he delivered Daozi to the Court of Justice; not one clerk or attendant dared watch or follow him. Hong was still in mourning, yet he alone bowed and took leave from the roadside, clinging to the carriage in tears—commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝召補鎮軍諮議參軍，以功封華容縣五等侯，累遷太尉左長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song summoned him to fill the post of Adviser to the General Who Guards the Army; for merit he was enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Huarong County and was promoted in succession to Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song summoned him as Adviser to the General Who Guards the Army; for his service he received the fifth-rank marquisate of Huarong and rose in time to Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 從北征，前鋒已平洛陽，而未遣九錫，弘銜使還都諷朝廷。

translations.literal: On the northern campaign the vanguard had already pacified Luoyang, yet the Nine Bestowments had not been sent; Hong, bearing an envoy's charge, returned to the capital to hint at the court.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaign the vanguard had already taken Luoyang, but the Nine Bestowments had not yet been granted; Hong returned to the capital on embassy to nudge the court toward that step.

sentences.zh: 時劉穆之掌留任，而旨乃從北來，穆之愧懼發病，遂卒。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Muzhi held the duties left behind in the capital, yet the imperial intent came from the north; Muzhi, ashamed and afraid, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi was then in charge at the capital, but the emperor's intent arrived from the north; stricken with shame and fear, Muzhi fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 宋國建，為尚書僕射掌選，領彭城太守。

translations.literal: When the state of Song was established he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing in charge of appointments and concurrently Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song state was founded he became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with charge of appointments, and also served as Administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 奏彈世子左衛率謝靈運，為軍人桂興淫其嬖妾，靈運殺興棄屍洪流，御史中丞王准之曾不彈舉。

translations.literal: He memorialized to impeach Xie Lingyun, Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, because the soldier Gui Xing had violated his favorite concubine and Lingyun killed Xing and cast the corpse into the rushing stream; the Imperial Censor Wang Zhunzhi had never impeached or reported it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted an impeachment of Xie Lingyun, Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard: a soldier named Gui Xing had violated Lingyun's favorite concubine, and Lingyun killed him and threw the body into the torrent—yet Imperial Censor Wang Zhunzhi had never reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 武帝答曰：「端右肅正風軌，誠副所期，自今以為永制。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu replied: "The right-hand ministers have rectified custom and truly fulfilled what was hoped; from now on let this be the permanent rule.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu answered: "You at the right hand of government have set the tone straight and truly met my hopes; let this stand as permanent practice from this day forward.

sentences.zh: 」於是免靈運官。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Lingyun was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Lingyun was then stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 後遷江州刺史，省賦簡役，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Jiang Province, reduced levies and simplified corvée, and the people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Inspector of Jiang Province, where he cut taxes and eased labor; the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 六年，弘又上表陳彭城王宜入輔，並求解州，義康由是代弘為司徒，與之分錄。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Hong again submitted a memorial stating that the Prince of Pengcheng ought to enter as assistant to the throne, and also asked to be relieved of the inspectorate; Yikang therefore replaced Hong as Minister of Education and shared with him the chief records.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Hong again memorialized that the Prince of Pengcheng should enter court as regent, and asked to surrender the inspectorate; Yikang replaced him as Minister of Education and shared the chief records with him.

sentences.zh: 弘又辭分錄。

translations.literal: Hong again declined the shared records.
translations.idiomatic: Hong again declined to share the records.

sentences.zh: 弘博練政體，留心庶事，斟酌時宜，每存優允。

translations.literal: Hong was broadly practiced in the body of government and attentive to common affairs; weighing the needs of the time, he always preserved leniency and fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was thoroughly versed in governance and attentive to everyday affairs; weighing each moment's needs, he always favored clemency and fair dealing.

sentences.zh: 與八座丞郎疏曰：「同伍犯法，無人士不罪之科，然每至詰謫，輒有請訴。

translations.literal: In a memorial to the Eight Seats and their clerks he said: "When men of the same ward break the law, there is no statute that does not punish the head of household, yet whenever inquiry and censure come, there are always petitions for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial to the Eight Seats and their clerks he wrote: "When members of the same ward violate the law, the head of household is always liable—yet at every inquiry petitions for mercy pour in.

sentences.zh: 若常垂恩宥，則法廢不行，依事糾責，則物以為苦。

translations.literal: If favor is constantly extended, the law fails and is not enforced; if matters are pursued and blame assigned, people find it bitter.
translations.idiomatic: Show constant leniency and the law ceases to bite; pursue every case to the letter and the people cry hardship.

sentences.zh: 恐宜更為其制。

translations.literal: I fear a new regulation should be made for this.
translations.idiomatic: I believe a new rule is needed here.

sentences.zh: 」時議多不同，弘以為：

translations.literal: " At the time many in discussion differed; Hong held that:
translations.idiomatic: " Opinion at the time was divided; Hong argued thus:

sentences.zh: 謂之人士，便無庶人之坐；

translations.literal: Call them men of standing, and they should not bear the commoner's penalty;
translations.idiomatic: Once you call someone a man of standing, he should not suffer the commoner's punishment;

sentences.zh: 署為庶人，輒受人士之罰，不其頗歟？

translations.literal: mark them as commoners and they immediately receive the punishment of men of standing—is this not excessive?
translations.idiomatic: yet label them commoners and they at once incur the penalties reserved for men of standing—is that not absurd?

sentences.zh: 謂人士可不受同伍之謫，取罪其奴客，庸何傷邪？

translations.literal: Say that men of standing need not accept the ward's censure and instead assign guilt to their slaves and clients—what harm in that?
translations.idiomatic: Let men of standing escape ward punishment and shift blame to their slaves and retainers—where is the injury in that?

sentences.zh: 無奴客，可令輸贖。

translations.literal: If they have no slaves or clients, let them pay a ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Those without slaves or clients may redeem the penalty instead.

sentences.zh: 有修身閭閻，與群小實隔，又或無奴僮，為眾所明者，官長二千石便親臨列上，依事遣判。

translations.literal: Again, those who cultivate themselves in the lanes and are in truth separated from the rabble, or who have no bondsmen yet are known to all, should have the local magistrate of two-thousand-bushel rank come in person to list them and send judgment according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Again, where a man keeps his conduct clean in the neighborhood and stands apart from the rabble—or has no bondsmen yet is known to all—the local magistrate of two-thousand-bushel rank should come in person, enter his name on the rolls, and decide the case on its merits.

sentences.zh: 又主守偷五疋，常偷四十疋，並加大辟。

translations.literal: Also, for a chief clerk who steals five bolts and a regular clerk who steals forty bolts, both were to receive the great execution.
translations.idiomatic: The existing rule also imposed death on a chief clerk who stole five bolts of cloth and on a regular clerk who stole forty.

sentences.zh: 議者咸以為重。

translations.literal: Discussants all thought this heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Those who debated the matter all judged the penalty too harsh.

sentences.zh: 弘以為：

translations.literal: Hong held that:
translations.idiomatic: Hong proposed instead:

sentences.zh: 小吏無知，臨財易昧。

translations.literal: Petty clerks lack understanding; faced with wealth they easily lose clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Petty clerks are ignorant men; set before money, their judgment clouds.

sentences.zh: 或由疏慢，事蹈重科。

translations.literal: Some through carelessness tread into the grave statute.
translations.idiomatic: Some stumble through negligence into capital crime.

sentences.zh: 宜進主守偷十疋，常偷五十疋死，四十疋降以補兵。

translations.literal: It is fitting to advance the threshold: a chief clerk who steals ten bolts and a regular clerk who steals fifty bolts die; at forty bolts reduce the sentence to conscription.
translations.idiomatic: Raise the thresholds: death for a chief clerk at ten bolts and a regular clerk at fifty; at forty bolts commute to military service.

sentences.zh: 至於官長以上，荷蒙榮祿，冒利五疋乃已為弘，士人至此，何容復加哀矜。

translations.literal: As for officials of magistrate rank and above, bearing honored stipends, to take profit of five bolts is already magnanimity—when a man of standing reaches this point, how can one still add pity?
translations.idiomatic: For magistrates and above, who enjoy honored stipends, stealing even five bolts already merits no mercy—when a gentleman sinks so low, what room remains for pity?

sentences.zh: 且此輩人士可殺不可謫，謂宜奏聞，決之聖旨。

translations.literal: Moreover, such men of standing may be killed but not censured; I hold that this should be reported to the throne and decided by the sacred intent.
translations.idiomatic: Such men of standing may be executed but should not be merely censured; this ought to be reported upward and left to the emperor's judgment.

sentences.zh: 文帝從弘議。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen followed Hong's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen adopted Hong's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 弘又上言：「舊制，人年十三半役，十六全役。

translations.literal: Hong also submitted: "Under the old system, at age thirteen one served half corvée and at sixteen full corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also memorialized: "Under the old rule, thirteen-year-olds served half labor and sixteen-year-olds full labor.

sentences.zh: 今四方無事，應存消息。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are without incident; we should preserve relief.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is at peace on every side; we should allow some easing.

sentences.zh: 請以十五至十六為半丁，十七為全丁。

translations.literal: I ask that fifteen to sixteen be half laborers and seventeen full laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Let fifteen and sixteen count as half laborers, and seventeen as full.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及弟曇首亡，文帝嗟悼不已，見弘流涕歔欷，弘斂容而已。

translations.literal: When his younger brother Tanshou died, Emperor Wen sighed in grief without end; seeing Hong he wept and sobbed, but Hong merely composed his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Tanshou died, Emperor Wen mourned without cease; meeting Hong he wept aloud, but Hong only composed his face.

sentences.zh: 既而彭城王義康言於帝曰：「曇首既為家寶，又為國器，弘情不稱，何也？

translations.literal: Presently the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang said to the emperor: "Tanshou was both a family treasure and a national vessel—why does Hong's feeling not match?
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang said to the emperor: "Tanshou was treasure to the clan and a pillar of the state—why does Hong's grief seem so slight?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「賢者意不可度。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The mind of the worthy cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "A worthy man's heart cannot be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 」其見體亮如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the understanding shown him.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the trust the throne placed in him.

sentences.zh: 九年進位太保，領中書監，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was advanced to Grand Mentor and made Director of the Secretariat; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to Grand Mentor and Director of the Secretariat; his other offices were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 其年薨。

translations.literal: That same year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the same year.

sentences.zh: 贈太保、中書監，給節，加羽葆、鼓吹，增班劍為六十人。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Mentor and Director of the Secretariat, granted the staff of office, added feather canopy and martial music, and his guard of swords was increased to sixty men.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he received the titles Grand Mentor and Director of the Secretariat, the staff of office, feather canopy and martial music, and an escort of sixty sword-bearers.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文昭公，配食武帝廟庭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Wen of Zhaogong, with sacrifice in the temple hall of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Duke Wen of Zhaogong and granted a place in Emperor Wu's temple.

sentences.zh: 弘既人望所宗，造次必存禮法。

translations.literal: Hong was the man to whom public expectation looked; even in haste he always preserved ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was a man the realm looked up to; even in haste he never abandoned ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 凡動止施為及書翰儀體，後人皆依放之，謂為王太保家法。

translations.literal: Whatever he did or wrote, and every form of correspondence and ceremony, later men all modeled themselves on it, calling it the household law of Grand Mentor Wang.
translations.idiomatic: His conduct, his letters, his ceremonial forms—later generations all took them as models, calling them the household law of Grand Mentor Wang.

sentences.zh: 雖曆藩輔，而不營財利，薨亡之後，家無餘業。

translations.literal: Though he served repeatedly as frontier minister and assistant, he did not pursue wealth; after his death the family had no surplus estate.
translations.idiomatic: Though he long held high provincial and court posts, he never chased profit; when he died the household held nothing extra.

sentences.zh: 而輕率少威儀。

translations.literal: Yet he was light and careless and lacked dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could be flippant and lacked gravitas.

sentences.zh: 客有疑其諱者，弘曰：「家諱與蘇子高同。

translations.literal: A guest doubted his taboo name; Hong said: "My family's taboo is the same as Su Zigao's.
translations.idiomatic: When a guest questioned his taboo name, Hong said: "Our family taboo matches that of Su Zigao.

sentences.zh: 」性褊隘，人有忤意，輒加詈辱。

translations.literal: " By nature he was narrow; when anyone crossed his will he at once cursed and shamed them.
translations.idiomatic: " He was touchy by nature; anyone who offended him was met with abuse.

sentences.zh: 少嘗摴蒱公城子野舍，及後當權，有人就弘求縣。

translations.literal: In youth he once played pitch-pot at Gong Chengye's house; later when he held power, someone came to Hong seeking a county post.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he had once gambled at pitch-pot in Gong Chengye's house; when he later held power, a man came seeking a county appointment.

sentences.zh: 此人嘗以蒱戲得罪，弘詰之曰：「君得錢會戲，何用祿為。

translations.literal: This man had once been punished for gambling; Hong questioned him: "You know how to win at games—what need have you of salary?
translations.idiomatic: The man had once been punished for gambling; Hong demanded: "You can win at games—why do you need an official salary?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「不審公城子野何所在。

translations.literal: " He answered: "I wonder where Gong Chengye is now.
translations.idiomatic: " The man replied: "I wonder where Gong Chengye is nowadays.

sentences.zh: 」弘默然。

translations.literal: " Hong fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Hong said nothing.

sentences.zh: 自領選及當朝總錄，將加榮爵於人者，每先呵責譴辱之，然後施行；

translations.literal: From the time he took charge of appointments until he held the chief records of the court, whenever he was about to add honor and rank to someone he first berated and shamed them, then carried it out;
translations.idiomatic: From his tenure in appointments through his years at the head of court records, whenever he was to grant rank or honor he first scolded and humiliated the recipient, then bestowed the favor;

sentences.zh: 若美相盼接語欣歡者，必無所諧。

translations.literal: if he looked kindly and received them with glad words, they were sure to gain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: those who met him with pleasant words and smiling faces invariably went away empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 人問其故，答曰：「王爵既加於人，又相撫勞，便成與主分功，此所謂奸以事君者也。

translations.literal: When asked the reason he answered: "Once a princely rank is added to a man and one also consoles and toils for him, it becomes sharing merit with the sovereign—this is what is called serving the ruler with cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he answered: "Grant a man noble rank and then soothe him with kind words, and you have shared the sovereign's merit with him—that is what people call serving the throne by guile.

sentences.zh: 若求者絕官敘之分，既無以為惠，又不微借顏色，即大成怨府，亦鄙薄所不任。

translations.literal: If the seeker cuts off the distinction of official rank, there is no way to show favor, yet if one does not even lend a little color to the face, that makes a great store of resentment—and that too is what base conduct cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: If the petitioner expects rank, you cannot truly favor him; yet refuse even a civil word and you breed lasting resentment—behavior too coarse for a gentleman to bear.

sentences.zh: 」問者悅伏。

translations.literal: " The questioner was pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " His interlocutor was convinced.

sentences.zh: 子錫嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 子 錫

translations.literal: Son Xi
translations.idiomatic: Son Xi

sentences.zh: 錫字寡光，位太子左衛率、江夏內史，高自位遇。

translations.literal: Xi, styled Guanguang, held the posts of Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Interior Minister of Jiangxia; he held himself high in rank and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, courtesy name Guanguang, served as Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Interior Minister of Jiangxia; he carried himself as though his station were above others.

sentences.zh: 太尉江夏王義恭當朝，錫箕踞大坐，殆無推敬。

translations.literal: When Grand Commandant the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong held the court, Xi sat sprawling with legs spread, scarcely showing deference.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, as Grand Commandant, presided at court, Xi sprawled in his seat with barely a show of respect.

sentences.zh: 卒，子僧亮嗣，齊受禪，降爵為侯。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Sengliang succeeded; when Qi received the abdication the rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his son Sengliang succeeded; when Qi took the throne the family rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 僧亮弟僧衍，位侍中。

translations.literal: Sengliang's younger brother Sengyan held the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sengliang's younger brother Sengyan served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 弘少子僧達。

translations.literal: Hong's youngest son Sengda.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's youngest son Sengda.

sentences.zh: 少子 僧達

translations.literal: Youngest son Sengda
translations.idiomatic: Youngest son Sengda

sentences.zh: 僧達幼聰敏，弘為揚州時，僧達六七歲，遇有通訟者，竊覽其辭，謂為有理。

translations.literal: Sengda was clever from childhood; when Hong was Inspector of Yang Province, Sengda was six or seven; once when someone came with a lawsuit he secretly read the petition and said it had reason.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda was precocious; when Hong was Inspector of Yang Province and Sengda was six or seven, a litigant arrived and the boy secretly read the petition and declared it just.

sentences.zh: 及大訟者亦進，弘意其小，留左右，僧達為申理，闇誦不失一句。

translations.literal: When the chief litigant also came in, Hong thought him too young and kept him at his side; Sengda argued the case for him, reciting it from memory without missing a sentence.
translations.idiomatic: When the principal litigant entered, Hong kept the boy nearby thinking him too young; Sengda pleaded the case for him, reciting every line from memory without error.

sentences.zh: 兄錫質訥乏風采。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xi was plain-spoken and lacked presence.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xi was dull of speech and without presence.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞僧達早慧，召見德陽殿，應對閑敏，上甚知之，妻以臨川王義慶女。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard that Sengda was early wise and summoned him to Deyang Hall; his replies were easy and quick; the emperor greatly noted him and gave him the Prince of Linchuan Yiqing's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen heard of Sengda's early brilliance and summoned him to Deyang Hall; his answers were fluent and apt, and the emperor took great notice of him and married him to a daughter of the Prince of Linchuan Yiqing.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善屬文，為太子舍人。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, was skilled at composition, and became Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved study from youth, wrote well, and became Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 坐屬疾而於揚列橋觀鬥鴨，為有司所糾，原不問。

translations.literal: He was punished for claiming illness yet watching duck fights on Yanglie Bridge; the censors reported him, but he was pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed illness yet went to Yanglie Bridge to watch duck fights; the censors reported him, but he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 性好鷹犬，與閭里少年相馳逐，又躬自屠牛。

translations.literal: By nature he loved hawks and hounds, raced with neighborhood youths, and personally butchered cattle.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hawking and hunting, raced with local youths, and even slaughtered cattle himself.

sentences.zh: 義慶聞之，令周旋沙門慧觀造而觀之，僧達陳書滿席，與論文義，慧觀酬答不暇，深相稱美。

translations.literal: When Yiqing heard this he sent the attendant monk Huiguan to visit and observe; Sengda's written compositions filled the mat, and when they discussed literary meaning Huiguan could not keep pace in reply and praised him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqing sent the monk Huiguan to observe him; Sengda's papers covered the mat, and in literary debate Huiguan could not keep up and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 訴家貧求郡，文帝欲以為秦郡。

translations.literal: He pleaded poverty and asked for a commandery; Emperor Wen wished to appoint him to Qin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading poverty, he asked for a prefecture; Emperor Wen meant to give him Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎庾仲文曰：「王弘子既不宜作秦郡，僧達亦不堪蒞人。

translations.literal: Director of the Office of Personnel Yu Zhongwen said: "Wang Hong's son is unfit for Qin commandery, and Sengda too cannot govern men.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Office of Personnel Yu Zhongwen said: "Wang Hong's son is no fit for Qin commandery, and Sengda cannot govern people either.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " So it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 遷太子洗馬，母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent and left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Groom of the Heir Apparent, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 與兄錫不協。

translations.literal: He was not on good terms with his elder brother Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Xi did not get along.

sentences.zh: 錫罷臨海郡還，送故及奉祿百萬以上，僧達一夕令奴輦取無餘。

translations.literal: When Xi left his post as Administrator of Linhai and returned, his parting gifts and salary totaled more than a million; in one night Sengda had his slaves carry it all off without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi returned from Linhai with parting gifts and salary exceeding a million cash, Sengda had his servants haul it all away in a single night.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為宣城太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he became Administrator of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed Administrator of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 性好遊獵，而山郡無事，僧達肆意馳騁，或五日三日方歸，受辭辯訟，多在獵所。

translations.literal: He loved roaming and hunting; in a mountain commandery with little business he rode at will, sometimes returning only after five or three days; receiving petitions and judging lawsuits, he often did so at the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hunting; in a quiet mountain prefecture he rode as he pleased, sometimes absent five days or three; lawsuits were often heard at the hunting grounds.

sentences.zh: 人或逢，不識，問府君所在。

translations.literal: When people met him and did not recognize him, they asked where the prefect was.
translations.idiomatic: Passersby who did not know him asked where the prefect was.

sentences.zh: 僧達且曰：「在近。

translations.literal: Sengda would say: "Nearby.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda would say: "Close at hand.

sentences.zh: 」其後徙義興。

translations.literal: " Later he was transferred to Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: " He was later transferred to Yixing.

sentences.zh: 及元凶弑立，孝武發尋陽，沈慶之謂人曰：「王僧達必來赴義。

translations.literal: When the crown prince regicide seized the throne, Emperor Xiaowu raised troops from Xunyang; Shen Qingzhi said to others: "Wang Sengda will surely come to the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince regicide took the throne, Emperor Xiaowu marched from Xunyang; Shen Qingzhi told others: "Wang Sengda will surely join the loyal cause.

sentences.zh: 」人問其所以，慶之曰：「虜馬飲江，王出赴難，見其在先帝前，議論開張，執意明決，以此言之，其必至也。

translations.literal: " When asked why, Qingzhi said: "When the barbarian horses drank at the river, Wang came to the crisis; I saw him before the late emperor, speaking boldly with clear, firm purpose—judging by that, he is sure to come.
translations.idiomatic: " Asked why, Qingzhi said: "When the enemy's horses reached the river, Wang stepped forward in the crisis; I saw him before the late emperor, speaking boldly with clear resolve—from that I know he will come.

sentences.zh: 」僧達尋至，孝武即以為長史。

translations.literal: " Sengda soon arrived, and Emperor Xiaowu at once made him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengda arrived soon after, and Xiaowu immediately made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 及即位，為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he became Vice Director of the Right Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu ascended the throne Sengda became Vice Director of the Right Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 僧達自負才地，一二年間便望宰相。

translations.literal: Sengda relied on his talent and station; within a year or two he looked to become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his talent and birth, within a year or two he expected the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 嘗答詔曰：「亡父亡祖，司徒司空。

translations.literal: Once answering an edict he said: "My late father and late grandfather were Minister of Education and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Replying once to an edict he wrote: "My late father and grandfather were Minister of Education and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 」其自負若此。

translations.literal: " Such was his pride.
translations.idiomatic: " So proud was he.

sentences.zh: 後為護軍將軍，不得志，乃求徐州，上不許。

translations.literal: Later he became General Who Protects the Army, was discontent, and asked for Xu Province; the emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as General Who Protects the Army, he grew restless and asked for Xu Province; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 固陳，乃以為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He pressed hard and was then made Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his request and was given Wu commandery instead.

sentences.zh: 時期歲五遷，彌不得意。

translations.literal: At the time he had been transferred five times in a year and was all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had been moved five times in a year and was more dissatisfied than ever.

sentences.zh: 吳郭西台寺多富沙門，僧達求須不稱意，乃遣主簿顧曠率門義劫寺內沙門竺法瑤得數百萬。

translations.literal: West of Wu city, Xitai Temple had many wealthy monks; Sengda's requests were not satisfied, so he sent his chief clerk Gu Kuang leading gate retainers to rob the monk Dharmayao inside the temple and obtained several million.
translations.idiomatic: West of Wu city stood Xitai Temple, rich in monks; when Sengda's demands went unmet he sent his chief clerk Gu Kuang with gate retainers to plunder the monk Dharmayao and seized several million cash.

sentences.zh: 荊、江反叛，加僧達置佐領兵。

translations.literal: When Jing and Jiang rebelled, Sengda was additionally ordered to set up aides and lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the rebellions in Jing and Jiang, Sengda was ordered to raise aides and lead troops.

sentences.zh: 台符聽置千人，而輒立三十隊，隊八十人。

translations.literal: The court warrant allowed a thousand men, yet he at once formed thirty companies of eighty men each.
translations.idiomatic: The court authorized a thousand men, but he immediately formed thirty companies of eighty each.

sentences.zh: 立宅于吳，多役功力，坐免官。

translations.literal: He built a mansion in Wu and used much corvée labor; for this he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mansion in Wu with heavy forced labor and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後孝武獨召見，傲然了不陳遜，唯張目而視。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowu summoned him alone; he was proud and offered no apology, only staring wide-eyed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaowu summoned him alone; he stood proud, offered no apology, and only stared back.

sentences.zh: 及出，帝歎曰：「王僧達非狂如何？

translations.literal: When he left, the emperor sighed: "If Wang Sengda is not mad, what is he?
translations.idiomatic: As Sengda left, the emperor sighed: "If Wang Sengda is not mad, then what is he?

sentences.zh: 乃戴面向天子。

translations.literal: He actually turned his face upward toward the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He actually stared up at the Son of Heaven with insolent eyes.

sentences.zh: 」後顏師伯詣之，僧達慨然曰：「大丈夫甯當玉碎，安可以沒沒求活。

translations.literal: " Later Yan Shibo visited him; Sengda said with feeling: "A great man would rather be jade shattered than live obscurely begging life.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Yan Shibo called on him; Sengda declared: "A true man would rather be shattered jade than live on in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 」師伯不答，逡巡便退。

translations.literal: " Shibo did not answer and withdrew after hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: " Shibo made no reply and withdrew uneasily.

sentences.zh: 先是，何尚之致仕，復膺朝命，於宅設八關齋，大集朝士，自行香，次至僧達曰：「願郎且放鷹犬，勿復遊獵。

translations.literal: Earlier, He Shangzhi had retired yet again received court appointment; at his house he held an Eight Gates fast and gathered many court gentlemen; he himself burned incense, and when his turn came to Sengda he said: "I hope the gentleman will release hawks and hounds and hunt no more.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier He Shangzhi had retired but was recalled; at home he held an Eight Gates fast and gathered court gentlemen. Passing the censer to Sengda he said: "Pray leave off hawking and hunting.

sentences.zh: 」僧達答曰：「家養一老狗，放無處去，已復還。

translations.literal: " Sengda answered: "My household keeps an old dog; let it go and it has nowhere to go—it comes back again.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengda answered: "My household keeps an old dog; turn it loose and it has nowhere to go—it always returns.

sentences.zh: 」尚之失色。

translations.literal: " Shangzhi changed color.
translations.idiomatic: " Shangzhi flushed.

sentences.zh: 大明中，以歸順功，封寧陵縣五等侯，累遷中書令。

translations.literal: In the Daming era, for merit in returning to allegiance he was enfeoffed Fifth-Rank Marquis of Ningling and was promoted in succession to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daming era he was enfeoffed fifth-rank Marquis of Ningling for loyalty and rose to Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎路瓊之，太后兄慶之孫也，宅與僧達門並。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Lu Qiongzhi was grandson of the empress dowager's elder brother Qingzhi; his house stood beside Sengda's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Lu Qiongzhi was grandson of the empress dowager's brother Qingzhi; his house faced Sengda's gate.

sentences.zh: 嘗盛車服詣僧達，僧達將獵，已改服。

translations.literal: Once he came in splendid carriage and dress; Sengda was about to hunt and had already changed clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qiongzhi came in splendid carriage and dress; Sengda was setting out to hunt and had already changed clothes.

sentences.zh: 瓊之就坐，僧達了不與語，謂曰：「身昔門下騶人路慶之者，是君何親？

translations.literal: Qiongzhi sat down; Sengda would not speak with him at all and said: "The runner Lu Qingzhi who was once at my gate—what kin is he to you?
translations.idiomatic: Qiongzhi sat down; Sengda refused to speak with him and asked: "Lu Qingzhi, the runner who once served at my gate—what relation is he to you?

sentences.zh: 」遂焚瓊之所坐床。

translations.literal: " Then he burned the couch Qiongzhi had sat on.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he burned the couch on which Qiongzhi had sat.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，泣涕於帝曰：「我尚在而人陵之，我死後乞食矣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and wept to the emperor: "While I still live men bully me; after I die I shall beg for food.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wept to the emperor: "While I still live men insult me; when I am dead my kin will beg in the streets.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「瓊之年少，無事詣王僧達門，見辱乃其宜耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Qiongzhi is young and came to Wang Sengda's gate without cause; to be insulted is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Qiongzhi is young and came uninvited to Wang Sengda's door; a rebuke was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 僧達貴公子，豈可以此加罪乎？

translations.literal: Sengda is a nobleman's son—how can he be punished for this?
translations.idiomatic: Sengda is a nobleman's son—how can this be grounds for punishment?

sentences.zh: 」太后又謂帝曰：「我終不與王僧達俱生。

translations.literal: " The empress dowager again told the emperor: "I will never live in the same age as Wang Sengda.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager told the emperor again: "I refuse to live in the same world as Wang Sengda.

sentences.zh: 」先是，南彭城蕃縣人高闍、沙門釋曇標、道方等共相誑惑，自言有鬼神龍鳳之瑞，常聞簫鼓音，與秣陵人藍宏期等謀為亂，又結殿中將軍苗乞食等起兵攻宮門。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Gao Ge of Fan county in Nan Pengcheng, the monk Shih Tanbiao, Daofang, and others had mutually deceived one another, claiming omens of spirits, dragons, and phoenixes and often hearing the sound of flutes and drums; with Lan Hongqi of Moling and others they plotted rebellion, and also joined Palace Guard Miao Qishi and others in raising troops to attack the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Gao Ge of Fan county in Nan Pengcheng, the monk Tanbiao, Daofang, and others had deluded the people with claims of dragon-and-phoenix omens and phantom music; with Lan Hongqi of Moling they plotted rebellion and joined Palace Guard Miao Qishi in an assault on the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 事發，凡党與死者數十人。

translations.literal: When the affair broke, several tens among the partisans died.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was exposed, several dozen conspirators were executed.

sentences.zh: 僧達屢經犯忤，上以為終無悛心，因高闍事陷之，收付廷尉，於獄賜死。

translations.literal: Sengda had repeatedly offended; the emperor thought he would never repent, and using the Gao Ge affair trapped him, seized him and handed him to the Court of Justice, and in prison granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda had repeatedly crossed the throne; believing he would never reform, the emperor used the Gao Ge case to entrap him, handed him to the Court of Justice, and had him executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 帝亦以為恨，謂江夏王義恭曰：「王僧達遂不免死，追思太保餘烈，使人慨然。

translations.literal: The emperor also felt regret and said to the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: "Wang Sengda could not escape death; recalling Grand Mentor's remaining glory, one is moved to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself felt regret and told the Prince of Jiangxia Yigong: "Wang Sengda could not be spared; thinking of Grand Mentor's legacy moves one to sigh.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔太保華容文昭公門爵國姻，一不貶絕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict declared that the gate rank, fief, and affinal ties of Grand Mentor Duke Wen of Zhaogong of Huarong were not to be cut off or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict then declared that the gate rank, fief, and marriage ties of Grand Mentor Duke Wen of Zhaogong of Huarong would not be diminished.

sentences.zh: 時有蘇寶者名寶生，本寒門，有文義之美，官至南台侍御史、江甯令，坐知高闍謀反，不即聞啟，亦伏誅。

translations.literal: At the time there was Su Bao, personal name Baosheng, originally of humble gate, with the beauty of literary meaning; he reached the posts of Attendant Censor of the Southern Office and Magistrate of Jiangning; he was punished for knowing of Gao Ge's plot to rebel yet not reporting at once, and was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time one Su Bao, born Baosheng, came from a humble family yet possessed literary grace; he rose to Attendant Censor of the Southern Office and Magistrate of Jiangning, but was executed for knowing of Gao Ge's rebellion and failing to report it promptly.

sentences.zh: 僧達子道琰，徙新安。

translations.literal: Sengda's son Daoyan was exiled to Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda's son Daoyan was exiled to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，為廬陵內史，未至郡，卒。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was Interior Minister of Luling; before reaching the commandery he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era he was appointed Interior Minister of Luling but died before reaching his post.

sentences.zh: 僧達孫 融

translations.literal: Sengda's grandson Rong
translations.idiomatic: Sengda's grandson Rong

sentences.zh: 融字元長，少而神明警慧。

translations.literal: Rong, styled Yuanchang, from youth was bright and keenly intelligent.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, courtesy name Yuanchang, was bright and precocious from childhood.

sentences.zh: 母臨川太守謝惠宣女，性敦敏，教融書學。

translations.literal: His mother was daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; she was earnest and quick, and taught Rong letters and learning.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a daughter of Xie Huixuan, Administrator of Linchuan; earnest and quick herself, she taught Rong reading and scholarship.

sentences.zh: 博涉有文才，從叔儉謂人曰：「此兒至四十，名位自然及祖。

translations.literal: Broadly read and possessed of literary talent, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "This boy at forty will naturally reach his grandfather's name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Well read and gifted in letters, his father's younger cousin Jian told others: "At forty this boy will naturally match his grandfather in rank and fame.

sentences.zh: 」舉秀才，累遷太子舍人。

translations.literal: " He was recommended as Presented Scholar and was promoted in succession to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " Recommended as Presented Scholar, he rose to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以父宦不通，弱年便欲紹興家業，啟齊武帝求自試，遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: Because his father's official career had not prospered, in weak years he wished to revive the family estate; he memorialized Emperor Wu of Qi asking to prove himself and was transferred to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His father's career had stalled; while still young Rong sought to revive the family fortunes, petitioned Emperor Wu of Qi for a trial appointment, and was made Secretary.

sentences.zh: 從叔儉初有儀同之授，贈儉詩及書，儉甚奇之，笑謂人曰：「穰侯印詎便可解。

translations.literal: When his father's younger cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian marveled greatly and smiling told others: "Can the seal of Ranghou really be taken off so soon?
translations.idiomatic: When his cousin Jian first received appointment as Equal to the Three Excellencies, Rong sent him a poem and letter; Jian was astonished and smiled: "So the seal of Ranghou can be handed over already?

sentences.zh: 」曆丹陽丞，中書郎。

translations.literal: " He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " He served as Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永明末，武帝欲北侵，使毛惠秀畫漢武北伐圖，融因此上疏，開張北侵之議。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongming era Emperor Wu wished to invade the north and had Mao Huixiu paint Emperor Wu of Han's northern campaign; Rong therefore submitted a memorial opening discussion of northern invasion.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming, when Emperor Wu planned a northern campaign and had Mao Huixiu paint Han Wudi's northern expedition, Rong submitted a memorial urging invasion.

sentences.zh: 圖成，上置琅邪城射堂壁上，遊幸輒觀焉。

translations.literal: When the painting was finished the emperor placed it on the wall of the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it whenever he toured.
translations.idiomatic: When the painting was finished the emperor hung it in the archery hall at Langya city and viewed it on every visit.

sentences.zh: 九年，芳林園禊宴，使融為曲水詩序，當時稱之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification feast, he had Rong compose the preface to the winding-water poems; men of the time praised it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at the Fanglin Garden spring purification, he had Rong write the preface to the winding-water poems; contemporaries praised it.

sentences.zh: 上以融才辯，使兼主客，接魏使房景高、宋弁。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Rong was talented and eloquent, had him additionally serve as Chief of Guests and receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, noting Rong's eloquence, also made him Chief of Guests to receive the Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.

sentences.zh: 弁見融年少，問：「主客年幾？

translations.literal: Bian saw Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?
translations.idiomatic: Bian saw that Rong was young and asked: "How old is the Chief of Guests?

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「五十之年，久踰其半。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Of fifty years, long past the half.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong replied: "Fifty years—well past the halfway mark.

sentences.zh: 」景高又云：「在北聞主客曲水詩序勝延年，實願一見。

translations.literal: " Jinggao also said: "In the north I heard the Chief of Guests' preface to the winding-water poems surpasses Yannian; I truly wish to see it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jinggao added: "In the north I heard your winding-water preface surpasses Yannian's—I long to see it.

sentences.zh: 」融乃示之。

translations.literal: " Rong then showed it.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong showed it to them.

sentences.zh: 後日，宋弁於瑤池堂謂融曰：「昔觀相如封禪，以知漢武之德，今覽王生詩序，用見齊主之盛。

translations.literal: Later, Song Bian at Yaochi Hall said to Rong: "Once reading Sima Xiangru's feng and shan text, one knew the virtue of Han Wu; now reading Master Wang's poem preface, one sees the splendor of the Qi lord.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Yaochi Hall Song Bian told Rong: "Reading Sima Xiangru's feng-shan text revealed Han Wudi's virtue; reading Master Wang's preface reveals our lord's splendor.

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「皇家盛明，豈直比蹤漢武，更慚鄙制，無以遠匹相如。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Our house's brilliance—how could it merely follow Han Wu? I am all the more ashamed of my crude composition; it cannot remotely match Xiangru.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong replied: "Our dynasty's brilliance far exceeds Han Wudi's; my humble piece cannot compare with Xiangru.

sentences.zh: 」上以魏所送馬不稱，使融問之曰：「秦西冀北，實多駿驥，而魏之良馬，乃駑不若，將旦旦信誓，有時而爽，駉駉之牧，遂不能嗣？

translations.literal: " The emperor, because the horses Wei sent were unworthy, had Rong ask: "West of Qin and north of Ji truly have many fine steeds, yet Wei's good horses are inferior nags—is the daily sworn faith sometimes broken, and the pastures of spirited horses no longer bred?
translations.idiomatic: " Because the horses Wei sent were poor, the emperor had Rong ask: "Qin west and Ji north abound in fine steeds, yet Wei's gifts are nags—has sworn faith broken, and the pastures failed?

sentences.zh: 」宋弁曰：「當是不習地土。

translations.literal: " Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil.
translations.idiomatic: " Song Bian said: "Perhaps they are unused to the soil here.

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「周穆馬跡遍於天下，若騏騮之性，因地而遷，則造父之策，有時而躓。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "King Mu of Zhou's horses' tracks covered the world; if the nature of qiji and juli shifts with land, then Zaofu's methods would sometimes stumble.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said: "King Mu's horses ranged the world; if fine breeds change with soil, then Zaofu's art would sometimes fail.

sentences.zh: 」弁曰：「王主客何為勤勤於千里？

translations.literal: " Bian said: "Why is the Chief of Guests so earnest about a thousand li?
translations.idiomatic: " Bian asked: "Why is the Chief of Guests so eager for horses from a thousand li away?

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「卿國既異其優劣，聊復相訪，若千里斯至，聖上當駕鼓車。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Since your state differs on quality, I merely inquire again; if they arrive from a thousand li, the sage emperor will drive the drum carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said: "Since your state disputes their quality, I ask again—if they truly come from afar, our emperor will drive the drum carriage to meet them.

sentences.zh: 」弁曰：「向意既須，必不能駕鼓車也。

translations.literal: " Bian said: "Since the intent is need, they surely cannot drive the drum carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Bian said: "If you truly need them, you surely will not send the drum carriage.

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「買死馬之骨，亦以郭隗之故。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Buying the bones of dead horses is also for Guo Kui's sake.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said: "Even buying dead horses' bones honors Guo Kui's memory.

sentences.zh: 」弁不能答。

translations.literal: " Bian could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Bian had no reply.

sentences.zh: 融躁于名利，自恃人地，三十內望為公輔。

translations.literal: Rong was impatient for fame and profit; relying on his birth and station, before thirty he looked to become chief minister and assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Rong hungered for fame and office; trusting in birth and rank, before thirty he expected the highest posts.

sentences.zh: 初為司徒法曹，詣王僧佑，因遇沈昭略，未相識。

translations.literal: At first as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education he called on Wang Sengyou and chanced to meet Shen Zhaolüe, whom he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career, as Law Clerk of the Minister of Education, he called on Wang Sengyou and met Shen Zhaolüe, a stranger to him.

sentences.zh: 昭略屢顧盼，謂主人曰：「是何年少？

translations.literal: Zhaolüe looked back repeatedly and said to the host: "What youth is this?
translations.idiomatic: Zhaolüe glanced back again and again and asked the host: "Who is this young man?

sentences.zh: 」融殊不平，謂曰：「僕出於扶桑，入于湯穀，照耀天下，誰雲不知，而卿此問？

translations.literal: " Rong was greatly displeased and said: "I come from Fusang and enter Tanggu, shining on all under heaven—who says they do not know, yet you ask this?
translations.idiomatic: " Rong was furious: "I rise from Fusang and set in Tanggu, shining over the world—who does not know me, that you should ask?

sentences.zh: 」昭略云：「不知許事，且食蛤蜊。

translations.literal: " Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of such things—let us eat clams.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhaolüe said: "I know nothing of that—let us eat clams instead.

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「物以群分，方以類聚，君長東隅，居然應嗜此族。

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Things group by kind, regions by class—you preside over the eastern corner and naturally should love this tribe.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong retorted: "Things flock by kind and regions by class—you rule the eastern corner and naturally favor this tribe.

sentences.zh: 」其高自標置如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his lofty self-regard.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his towering self-regard.

sentences.zh: 及為中書郎，嘗撫案歎曰：「為爾寂寂，鄧禹笑人。

translations.literal: When he was Gentleman of the Secretariat he once struck the desk and sighed: "For this silence, Deng Yu would laugh at me.
translations.idiomatic: As Gentleman of the Secretariat he once struck the desk and sighed: "In this obscurity even Deng Yu would laugh at me.

sentences.zh: 」行遇朱雀桁開，路人填塞，乃捶車壁曰：「車中乃可無七尺，車前豈可乏八騶。」

translations.literal: Passing the Vermilion Bird Bridge when it was open, the road was packed with people; he beat the carriage wall and said: "Inside the carriage there can be no seven-foot man; before the carriage there must be no lack of eight outrunners."
translations.idiomatic: When the Vermilion Bird Bridge opened and the road jammed with people, he hammered the carriage wall and cried: "A carriage should hold a seven-foot man; before it there must be no lack of eight outrunners."

sentences.zh: 及魏軍動，竟陵王子良于東府募人，板融甯朔將軍、軍主。

translations.literal: When Wei troops moved, the Prince of Jingling Ziliang at the Eastern Mansion recruited men and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei armies mobilized, the Prince of Jingling Ziliang recruited at the Eastern Mansion and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 融文辭捷速，有所造作，援筆可待，子良特相友好。

translations.literal: Rong's literary phrasing was quick; whatever he wrote he could finish at the brush; Ziliang was especially friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wrote with swift grace; whatever he undertook he finished at a stroke; Ziliang favored him especially.

sentences.zh: 晚節大習騎馬，招集江西傖楚數百人，並有幹用，融特為謀主。

translations.literal: In late years he greatly practiced horsemanship, gathered several hundred rough men of Jiang west and Chu, all capable, and Rong alone was their chief planner.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he took hard to horsemanship, gathered several hundred tough men from west of the river and Chu, all useful fighters, and made himself their chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 武帝病篤暫絕，子良在殿內，太孫未入，融戎服絳衫，於中書省合口斷東宮仗不得進，欲矯詔立子良。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang was in the palace hall and the heir had not entered; Rong in martial dress and scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate from entering, wishing to forge an edict and install Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu lay gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang remained in the palace while the heir had not entered; Rong in martial dress and scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate, intending to forge an edict and install Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 詔草已立，上重蘇，朝事委西昌侯鸞。

translations.literal: The draft edict was already written; the emperor recovered and court affairs were entrusted to the Marquis of Xichang Luan.
translations.idiomatic: The draft edict was already written; the emperor rallied and entrusted affairs to the Marquis of Xichang Luan.

sentences.zh: 梁武謂範雲曰：「左手據天下圖，右手刎其喉，愚夫不為。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang said to Fan Yun: "Left hand holding the map of all under heaven, right hand cutting its throat—no fool would do that.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang told Fan Yun: "Left hand on the empire's map, right hand at its throat—no fool would do that.

sentences.zh: 主上大漸，國家自有故事，道路籍籍，將有非常之舉，卿聞之乎？

translations.literal: The lord is failing; the state has its own precedents; on the roads there is clamor that something extraordinary will happen—have you heard?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is failing; the state has its own precedents; the roads buzz with talk of something extraordinary—have you heard?

sentences.zh: 」雲不敢答。

translations.literal: " Yun did not dare answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Yun dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝崩，融乃處分以子良兵禁諸門，西昌侯聞，急馳到雲龍門，不得進，乃曰：「有敕召我。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died; Rong then disposed troops with Ziliang's soldiers to seal the gates; the Marquis of Xichang heard and galloped to Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter; he then said: "There is an edict summoning me.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor died; Rong deployed Ziliang's troops to seal the gates; the Marquis of Xichang galloped to Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter and cried: "An edict summons me.

sentences.zh: 」仍排而入，奉太孫登殿，命左右扶出子良，指麾音響如鍾，殿內無不從命。

translations.literal: " He pushed in, escorted the heir to the throne, ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out; his commands rang like a bell and none in the hall disobeyed.
translations.idiomatic: " He forced his way in, escorted the heir to the throne, ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out; his commands rang like a bell and none in the hall disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 融知不遂，乃釋服還省，歎曰：「公誤我。」

translations.literal: Rong knew he would not succeed, put off his martial dress and returned to his office, and sighed: "The duke misled me."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had failed, Rong changed out of martial dress, returned to his office, and sighed: "The duke misled me."

sentences.zh: 郁林深怨融，即位十餘日，收下廷尉獄。

translations.literal: Emperor Yulin deeply resented Rong; more than ten days after taking the throne he seized him and put him in the Court of Justice prison.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yulin deeply hated Rong; within ten days of enthronement he seized him and cast him into the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 使中丞孔珪倚為奏曰：「融姿性剛險，立身浮競，動跡驚群，抗言異類。

translations.literal: He had the Censor Kong Gui draft the memorial on his behalf: "Rong's nature is hard and dangerous, his conduct floating and competitive; his movements startle the crowd and his bold words differ from the kind.
translations.idiomatic: He had Censor Kong Gui draft the impeachment: "Rong's nature is harsh and treacherous, his conduct restless and ambitious; his deeds startle the crowd and his words defy convention.

sentences.zh: 近塞外微塵，苦求將領，遂招納不逞，扇誘荒傖。

translations.literal: Lately at the frontier dust he bitterly sought command and thus recruited unruly men, inciting wild northerners.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, with dust on the frontier, he bitterly sought command and recruited unruly men, stirring up wild northerners.

sentences.zh: 狡弄威聲，專行權利，反復唇齒之間，傾動頰舌之內，威福自己，無所忌憚，誹謗朝政，曆毀王公。

translations.literal: Cunningly wielding threatening voice, exclusively exercising power and profit, back and forth between lips and teeth, shaking within cheek and tongue, authority and favor from himself, without dread; slandering court governance, repeatedly destroying kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He played at intimidation, grasped power for himself, whispered and shouted as he pleased, feared nothing, slandered the court, and repeatedly defamed princes and nobles.

sentences.zh: 謂己才流，無所推下，事暴遠近，使融依源據答。

translations.literal: He said his talent and class had none beneath him; the matter was exposed far and near; let Rong answer according to source and evidence.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed no man matched his talent and birth; the charges were known far and wide; let Rong answer point by point.

sentences.zh: 」融辭曰：「囚實頑蔽，觸行多愆。

translations.literal: " Rong replied: "The prisoner is indeed stubborn and blind; his conduct has many faults.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong replied: "The prisoner is indeed dull and erring; his conduct has many faults.

sentences.zh: 但夙忝門素，得奉教君子。

translations.literal: Yet from old I have disgraced my gate and lineage by receiving instruction from gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from youth I have borne my family's name and received instruction from gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 爰自總發，迄將立年，州閭鄉党，見許愚慎。

translations.literal: From first tying the hair until nearly the age of standing, in district and village my neighbors called me cautious.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood until nearly adulthood, neighbors in district and village called me prudent.

sentences.zh: 過蒙大行皇帝獎育之恩，又荷文皇帝識擢之重，司徒公賜預士林，安陸王曲垂盼接，前後陳伐虜之計，亦仰簡先朝。

translations.literal: I overly received the late Grand Emperor's nurturing favor and also bore the late Literary Emperor's recognition and promotion; the Minister of Education granted me place among the literati, the Prince of Anlu graciously received me; my plans for campaigning against the barbarians were also approved by the former court.
translations.idiomatic: I enjoyed the late Grand Emperor's nurturing favor and the late Literary Emperor's recognition; the Minister of Education admitted me to the literati, the Prince of Anlu favored me; my plans against the northern foe were also approved by the former court.

sentences.zh: 今段犬羊乍擾，令囚草撰符詔。

translations.literal: Now when the dogs and sheep suddenly stirred, the prisoner was ordered to draft edicts and warrants.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern barbarians suddenly stirred, I was ordered to draft edicts and warrants.

sentences.zh: 及司徒宣敕招募，同例非一，實以戎事不小，不敢承教。

translations.literal: Again the Minister of Education proclaimed orders to recruit; there were many like cases—not because military matters were small did I dare refuse instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education again proclaimed recruitment; others did the same—it was not because the war was minor that I refused.

sentences.zh: 續蒙軍號，賜使招集，銜敕而行，非敢虛扇。

translations.literal: I again received a military title and was granted orders to gather men; I carried the command and went—not daring to stir empty alarm.
translations.idiomatic: I received a military title and orders to gather troops; I carried out the command—I did not stir empty alarm.

sentences.zh: 且'張弄威聲'，應有形跡。

translations.literal: Moreover, 'cunningly wielding threatening voice' should have visible traces.
translations.idiomatic: As for 'playing at intimidation,' there should be visible evidence.

sentences.zh: '專行權利'，又無贓賄。

translations.literal: 'Exclusively exercising power and profit'—again there is no bribe.
translations.idiomatic: 'Grasping power for profit'—again, there is no bribe.

sentences.zh: '反復唇齒之間'，未審悉與誰言？

translations.literal: 'Back and forth between lips and teeth'—I do not know with whom all this was spoken?
translations.idiomatic: 'Whispering between lips and teeth'—with whom was all this spoken?

sentences.zh: '傾動頰舌之內'，不容都無主此。

translations.literal: 'Shaking within cheek and tongue'—surely there cannot be no one who presided over this?
translations.idiomatic: 'Shouting within cheek and tongue'—surely someone must have presided over it?

sentences.zh: 自上甘露頌及銀甕啟、三日詩序、接虜使語辭，竭思稱揚，得非誹謗。

translations.literal: From the Sweet Dew hymn upward, the silver-jar memorial, the three-day poem preface, and the words receiving the barbarian envoys—I exhausted thought in praise; how can this be slander?
translations.idiomatic: From the Sweet Dew hymn to the silver-jar memorial, the three-day poem preface, and my words with barbarian envoys—I exhausted myself in praise; how is that slander?

sentences.zh: 囚才分本劣，謬被策用，悚怍之情，夙宵兢惕，自循自省，並愧流言。

translations.literal: The prisoner's talent and measure are by nature inferior; wrongly chosen for use, my fearful shame day and night is vigilant; examining myself, I am ashamed before idle talk.
translations.idiomatic: My talent is by nature modest; wrongly placed in office, I tremble day and night; examining myself, I am ashamed before gossip.

sentences.zh: 伏惟明皇臨宇，普天蒙澤，戊寅赦恩，輕重必宥，百日曠期，始蒙旬日，一介罪身，獨嬰憲劾。

translations.literal: I bow that the bright emperor overlooks the realm and all heaven receives grace; the Wuyin amnesty must spare light and heavy alike, and the hundred-day grace period had only just granted ten days—a lone guilty body alone bears punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before the bright emperor whose grace covers the realm; the Wuyin amnesty spares light and heavy alike, and within the hundred-day grace I had barely ten days—a lone guilty man alone bears punishment.

sentences.zh: 」融被收，朋友部曲，參問北寺，相繼於道；

translations.literal: " When Rong was seized, friends and retainers came to inquire at North Temple one after another on the road;
translations.idiomatic: " When Rong was seized, friends and retainers lined the road to North Temple to inquire after him;

sentences.zh: 請救於子良，子良不敢救；

translations.literal: they asked Ziliang for rescue, and Ziliang did not dare rescue;
translations.idiomatic: they begged Ziliang to save him, but Ziliang dared not;

sentences.zh: 西昌侯固爭不得。

translations.literal: the Marquis of Xichang argued hard but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: the Marquis of Xichang argued fiercely but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 詔于獄賜死，時年二十七。

translations.literal: An edict granted death in prison; he was then twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered death in prison; he was twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 臨死歎曰：「我若不為百歲老母，當吐一言。

translations.literal: Facing death he sighed: "If not for my hundred-year-old mother, I would speak one word.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he sighed: "Were it not for my aged mother, I would speak one word.

sentences.zh: 」融意欲指斥帝在東宮時過失也。

translations.literal: Rong intended to denounce the emperor's faults when he was Eastern Palace heir.
translations.idiomatic: Rong meant to expose the emperor's misconduct from his days as heir.

sentences.zh: 先是，太學生會稽魏准，以才學為融所賞，既欲奉子良，而准鼓成其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, a Grand Academy student, was admired by Rong for talent and learning; wishing to support Ziliang, Zhun urged the matter on.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, a Grand Academy student admired by Rong for talent, wished to support Ziliang and pressed the plot forward.

sentences.zh: 太學生虞羲、丘國賓竊相謂曰：「竟陵才弱，王中書無斷，敗在眼中矣。

translations.literal: Grand Academy students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin whispered to each other: "The Prince of Jingling's talent is weak and Director of the Secretariat Wang lacks resolve—defeat is before our eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academy students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin whispered: "Jingling's talent is weak and Wang the Secretariat Director lacks resolve—defeat is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 」及融誅，召准入舍人省詰問，遂懼而死，舉體皆青，時人以准膽破。

translations.literal: " When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Attendants' Office for questioning; in fear he died, his whole body turning blue; men of the time said Zhun's gall had burst.
translations.idiomatic: " When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Attendants' Office for questioning; terror killed him—his whole body turned blue—and men said his gall had burst.

sentences.zh: 融文集行于時。

translations.literal: Rong's collected writings circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's collected writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 弟孺子 微

translations.literal: Younger brother Ruzi Wei
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Ruzi Wei

sentences.zh: 微字景玄，弘弟光祿大夫孺之子也。

translations.literal: Wei, styled Jingxuan, was son of Hong's younger brother Ru, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, courtesy name Jingxuan, was son of Hong's younger brother Ru, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善屬文，工書，兼解音律及醫方卜筮陰陽數術之事。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, was skilled at composition, practiced calligraphy, and also understood music, medicine, divination, and the arts of yin-yang and number.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, wrote well, practiced calligraphy, and also mastered music, medicine, divination, and the yin-yang arts.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝賜以名蓍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song bestowed on him famous yarrow stalks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Song gave him a set of famed yarrow stalks for divination.

sentences.zh: 初為始興王友，父憂去職。

translations.literal: At first he was Friend to the Prince of Shixing; on his father's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as Friend to the Prince of Shixing, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 微素無宦情，服闋，除南平王鑠右軍諮議參軍，仍為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Wei had never desired office; when mourning ended he was appointed Adviser to the Right Army of the Prince of Nanping Shuo and then Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had never sought office; after mourning he was made Adviser to the Right Army of the Prince of Nanping Shuo, then Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時兄遠免官歷年，微歎曰：「我兄無事而屏廢，我何得而叼忝踰分？

translations.literal: At the time his elder brother Yuan had been removed from office for years; Wei sighed: "My elder brother is idle without cause—how can I presumptuously exceed my measure?
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yuan had been idle without cause for years; Wei sighed: "My brother sits dismissed without fault—how can I presumptuously hold higher rank?

sentences.zh: 」文帝即以遠為光祿勳。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen at once made Yuan Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen at once restored Yuan as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 微為文好古，言頗抑揚，袁淑見之，謂為訴屈。

translations.literal: Wei's writing loved the antique and his language was often measured in rise and fall; when Yuan Shu saw it he called it an appeal of wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's prose favored antique style with measured cadence; Yuan Shu read it and called it a plea against injustice.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書江湛舉微為吏部郎，微確乎不拔。

translations.literal: Director of the Office of Personnel Jiang Zhan recommended Wei as Director of the Office of Personnel; Wei firmly would not be pulled out.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Office of Personnel Jiang Zhan recommended Wei for that same post; Wei steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 時論者或云微之見舉，廬江何偃亦參其議。

translations.literal: Discussants at the time sometimes said that in Wei's recommendation, He Yan of Lujiang also shared in the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that when Wei was recommended, He Yan of Lujiang had also joined the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 偃慮為微所咎，與之書自陳。

translations.literal: Yan feared Wei would blame him and wrote a letter explaining himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yan feared Wei would resent him and wrote to explain himself.

sentences.zh: 微報書深言塵外之適。

translations.literal: Wei replied in a letter deeply speaking of the suitability of life beyond the dust.
translations.idiomatic: Wei replied at length on the joys of life beyond office.

sentences.zh: 其從弟僧綽宣文帝旨使就職，因留之宿。

translations.literal: His younger male cousin Sengchuo conveyed Emperor Wen's intent that he take office, and therefore kept him overnight.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Sengchuo brought Emperor Wen's order that he take office and kept him overnight.

sentences.zh: 微妙解天文，知當有大故，獨與僧綽仰視，謂曰：「此上不欺人，非智者其孰能免之。

translations.literal: Wei subtly understood astronomy and knew there would soon be a great change; alone with Sengchuo he looked upward and said: "He above does not deceive men—who but the wise can escape it?
translations.idiomatic: Wei understood astronomy and knew calamity was near; alone with Sengchuo he looked skyward and said: "Heaven does not deceive—who but the wise can escape what comes?

sentences.zh: 」遂辭不就。

translations.literal: " He then declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He declined and would not take the post.

sentences.zh: 尋有元凶之變。

translations.literal: Soon there was the crown prince regicide's upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Soon came the crown prince regicide's coup.

sentences.zh: 微常住門屋一間，尋書玩古，遂足不履地。

translations.literal: Wei always lived in one room at the gate, seeking books and enjoying antiquity; his feet did not tread the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wei lived in a single gate-room, reading antiquity; he scarcely set foot outside.

sentences.zh: 終日端坐，床席皆生塵埃，唯當坐處獨淨。

translations.literal: All day he sat upright; bed and mat grew dusty, only the place where he sat remained clean.
translations.idiomatic: He sat upright all day; bed and mat gathered dust—only his seat stayed clean.

sentences.zh: 弟僧謙亦有才譽，為太子舍人，遇疾，微躬自處療，而僧謙服藥失度，遂卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Sengqian also had talent and reputation and was Attendant of the Heir Apparent; when he fell ill Wei personally treated him, yet Sengqian took medicine beyond measure and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sengqian, also talented, served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent; when Sengqian fell ill Wei treated him himself, but Sengqian overdosed on medicine and died.

sentences.zh: 深自咎恨，發病不復自療，哀痛僧謙不能已，以書告靈。

translations.literal: Deeply blaming himself, he fell ill and no longer treated himself; grieving Sengqian without end, he wrote a letter telling the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Blaming himself deeply, he fell ill and ceased treating himself; unable to end his grief for Sengqian, he wrote to his spirit.

sentences.zh: 僧謙卒後四旬而微終，遺令薄葬，不設車需旐鼓挽之屬，施五尺床為靈，二宿便毀，以常所彈琴置床上，何長史偃來，以琴與之。

translations.literal: Forty days after Sengqian's death Wei died; his final instructions were for a plain burial without carriage cloth, pennants, drums, or mourning escort; a five-foot bed served as the spirit seat and was destroyed after two nights; the zither he always played was placed on the bed; when Chief Clerk He Yan came, the zither was given to him.
translations.idiomatic: Forty days after Sengqian's death Wei died; he ordered a plain burial without mourning pomp; a five-foot bed served as the spirit seat and was destroyed after two nights; his zither was placed upon it and given to Chief Clerk He Yan when he came.

sentences.zh: 無子，家人遵之。

translations.literal: He had no sons; the household followed this.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons; the household obeyed his wishes.

sentences.zh: 所著文集傳於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings were transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings passed down in the world.

sentences.zh: 贈秘書監。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 微兄 遠

translations.literal: Wei's elder brother Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Wei's elder brother Yuan

sentences.zh: 微兄遠字景舒，位光祿勳。

translations.literal: Wei's elder brother Yuan, styled Jingshu, held the post of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's elder brother Yuan, courtesy name Jingshu, served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時人謂遠如屏風，屈曲從俗，能蔽風露。

translations.literal: Men of the time said Yuan was like a folding screen—bending to follow custom, able to shield against wind and dew.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries said Yuan was like a folding screen—bending with custom, shielding against wind and dew.

sentences.zh: 言能不乖物理也。

translations.literal: The saying meant he could not violate physical principle.
translations.idiomatic: The saying meant he never fought the way things are.

sentences.zh: 遠子僧佑字胤宗，幼聰悟，叔父微撫其首曰：「兒神明意用，當不作率爾人。

translations.literal: Yuan's son Sengyou, styled Yinzong, was clever from childhood; his uncle Wei stroked his head and said: "The boy's spirit and intent—he will not become a careless man.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's son Sengyou, courtesy name Yinzong, was clever as a child; his uncle Wei stroked his head and said: "This boy's mind is bright—he will not be a careless man.

sentences.zh: 」雅為從兄儉所重，每鳴笳列騶到其門候之，僧佑輒稱疾不前。

translations.literal: " He was always valued by his older male cousin Jian, who each time with horn and outrunners came to his gate to wait; Sengyou always pleaded illness and would not go forward.
translations.idiomatic: " His cousin Jian prized him and often came to his gate with horn and outrunners; Sengyou always pleaded illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「此吾之所望於若人也。

translations.literal: Jian said: "This is what I hoped for in you.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said: "That is exactly what I hoped of you.

sentences.zh: 」世皆推儉之愛名德，而重僧佑之不趨勢也。

translations.literal: " The world all praised Jian's love of name and virtue and valued Sengyou's not rushing toward power.
translations.idiomatic: " The world praised Jian for loving worth and Sengyou for refusing to chase power.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，頻經憂，居喪至孝。

translations.literal: Before weak crown he repeatedly passed through mourning and in mourning was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he endured repeated bereavements and mourned with supreme filiality.

sentences.zh: 服闋，發落略盡，殆不立冠帽。

translations.literal: When mourning ended his hair had nearly all fallen; he could scarcely wear cap or hat.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended his hair had nearly all fallen out; he could scarcely wear cap or hat.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，為驃騎法曹，羸瘠不堪受命。

translations.literal: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he became Law Clerk to the Cavalry General but was too emaciated to accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Presented Scholar, he was made Law Clerk to the Cavalry General but was too frail to serve.

sentences.zh: 雅好博古，善老、莊，不尚繁華。

translations.literal: He elegantly loved antiquity, favored Laozi and Zhuangzi, and did not esteem extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: He loved antiquity, favored Laozi and Zhuangzi, and scorned extravagance.

sentences.zh: 工草隸，善鼓琴，亭然獨立，不交當世。

translations.literal: Skilled in cursive and clerical script and in playing the zither, he stood apart and did not associate with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in cursive and clerical script and in the zither, he stood apart and kept aloof from the world.

sentences.zh: 沛國劉瓛聞風而悅，上書薦之。

translations.literal: Liu Huan of Pei, hearing his reputation, was pleased and submitted a memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan of Pei, hearing his reputation, was delighted and memorialized recommending him.

sentences.zh: 為著作佐郎，遷司空祭酒，謝病不與公卿遊。

translations.literal: He was Assistant Editor and was transferred to Libationer of the Minister of Works; he pleaded illness and did not travel with dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He became Assistant Editor, then Libationer of the Minister of Works; pleading illness, he avoided the company of high officials.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝謂王儉曰：「卿從可謂朝隱。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao of Qi said to Wang Jian: "Your cousin may be called a court recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao of Qi told Wang Jian: "Your cousin is a recluse at court.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「臣從非敢妄同高人，直是愛閑多病耳。

translations.literal: " He answered: "My cousin does not dare rashly match lofty men—he simply loves leisure and is much ill.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian answered: "My cousin does not pretend to lofty reclusion—he simply loves leisure and is often ill.

sentences.zh: 」經贈儉詩云：「汝家在市門，我家在南郭；

translations.literal: " Once in a poem to Jian he wrote: "Your house is at the market gate, mine south of the wall;
translations.idiomatic: " Once he wrote Jian: "Your house stands at the market gate, mine south of the wall;

sentences.zh: 汝家饒賓侶，我家多鳥雀。

translations.literal: your house is rich in guest companions, mine in birds and sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: yours abounds in guests, mine in birds and sparrows.

sentences.zh: 」儉時聲高一代，賓客填門，僧佑不為之屈，時人嘉之。

translations.literal: " Jian's fame then filled a generation and guests filled his gate; Sengyou did not yield to this, and men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian's fame then filled the age and guests thronged his gate; Sengyou would not bend to it, and men praised him.

sentences.zh: 稍遷晉安王文學，而陳郡袁利為友，時人以為妙選。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Literary Companion to the Prince of Jin'an, and Yuan Li of Chen commandery was his Friend—men of the time considered this a fine pairing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Literary Companion to the Prince of Jin'an; Yuan Li of Chen was his Friend—a pairing men called inspired.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝數閱武，僧佑獻講武賦，王儉借觀不與。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Qi often reviewed martial arts; Sengyou submitted a "Discourse on Martial Review"; Wang Jian asked to borrow and view it but he would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Qi often reviewed troops; Sengyou submitted a Discourse on Martial Review; Wang Jian asked to read it but he refused.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良聞其工琴，於座取琴進之，不從命。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingling Ziliang heard he was skilled at the zither; at a gathering he took a zither and offered it; Sengyou did not obey the command.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jingling Ziliang, hearing of his zither, offered one at a gathering; Sengyou refused.

sentences.zh: 永明末，為太子中舍人，在直屬疾，不待對人輒去。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongming he was Attendant of the Heir Apparent; while on duty he fell ill and left before facing anyone.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongming he was Attendant of the Heir Apparent; on duty he took ill and left without awaiting audience.

sentences.zh: 中丞沈約彈之云：「肆情運氣，不顧朝典，揚眉闊步，直轡高驅。

translations.literal: Censor Shen Yue impeached him: "He indulges mood at will, heedless of court statute; eyebrows raised, stride broad, reins straight, carriage high.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shen Yue impeached him: "He indulges his mood heedless of court law—brows raised, stride wide, reins taut, carriage high.

sentences.zh: 」坐贖論。

translations.literal: " He was punished by redemption.
translations.idiomatic: " He was fined in lieu of punishment.

sentences.zh: 時何點、王思遠之徒請交，並不降意。

translations.literal: At the time He Dian, Wang Siyuan, and others asked for acquaintance; he did not lower his intent.
