translations.idiomatic: He Dian, Wang Siyuan, and others sought his friendship; he would not condescend.

sentences.zh: 自天子至於侯伯，未嘗與一人遊。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to marquises and earls, he never kept company with a single man.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven to marquises and earls, he kept company with no one.

sentences.zh: 卒于黃門郎。

translations.literal: He died as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 子籍。

translations.literal: Son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Son Ji.

sentences.zh: 籍字文海，仕齊為余杭令，政化如神，善於擿伏，自下莫能欺也。

translations.literal: Ji, styled Wenhai, served Qi as Magistrate of Yuhang; his governance was like spirit, skilled at exposing hidden wrong; those below could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, courtesy name Wenhai, served Qi as Magistrate of Yuhang; his rule seemed almost supernatural, and he exposed hidden crimes so that none below could deceive him.

sentences.zh: 性頗不儉，俄然為百姓所訟。

translations.literal: By nature he was quite not frugal; soon the common people sued him.
translations.idiomatic: He was not frugal by nature; soon the people brought suit against him.

sentences.zh: 又為錢唐縣，下車布政，咸謂數十年來未之有也。

translations.literal: Again as Magistrate of Qiantang, from the day he took office his governance was called unmatched in several decades.
translations.idiomatic: As Magistrate of Qiantang, from his first day in office his governance was called unmatched in decades.

sentences.zh: 籍好學，有才氣，為詩慕謝靈運。

translations.literal: Ji loved learning and had literary spirit; in poetry he admired Xie Lingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Ji loved learning and had literary talent; in poetry he modeled himself on Xie Lingyun.

sentences.zh: 至其合也，殆無愧色。

translations.literal: When he matched him, there was nearly no look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: When he matched Lingyun's level, he scarcely blushed.

sentences.zh: 時人咸謂康樂之有王籍，如仲尼之有丘明，老聃之有嚴周。

translations.literal: Men of the time all said that Kangle had Wang Ji as Zhongni had Qiuming and Laozi had Yan Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time said that for Kangle's poetry there was Wang Ji, as Confucius had Qiu Ming and Laozi had Yan Zhou.

sentences.zh: 梁天監中，為輕車湘東王諮議參軍，隨府會稽郡。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era of Liang he was Adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong and followed the princely establishment to Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang's Tianjian era he was Adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong and followed the establishment to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 至若邪溪賦詩云：「蟬噪林逾靜，鳥鳴山更幽。

translations.literal: At Ruoye Stream he composed a poem: "Cicadas cry—the grove grows stiller; birds sing—the mountain grows deeper.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruoye Stream he wrote: "Cicadas cry—the grove grows stiller; birds sing—the mountain grows deeper.

sentences.zh: 」劉孺見之，擊節不能已已。

translations.literal: " Liu Ru saw it and beat time without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Ru saw it and beat time in endless admiration.

sentences.zh: 以公事免。

translations.literal: He was removed for official business.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed over an official matter.

sentences.zh: 及為中散大夫，彌忽忽不樂，乃至徒行市道，不擇交遊。

translations.literal: When he became Grand Master of the Palace, he grew all the more restless and unhappy, even walking the market on foot without choosing companions.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Master of the Palace he grew restless and unhappy, even walking the streets on foot without choosing his company.

sentences.zh: 有時塗中見相識，輒以笠傘覆面。

translations.literal: Sometimes on the road he saw an acquaintance and covered his face with hat and umbrella.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes on the road he saw an acquaintance and hid his face beneath hat and umbrella.

sentences.zh: 後為作唐侯相，小邑寡事，彌不樂，不理縣事。

translations.literal: Later he became Marquis of Zuotang; the small territory had little business and he was all the more unhappy, not managing county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Marquis of Zuotang; the tiny fief had little to do and he was unhappier still, ignoring county affairs.

sentences.zh: 人有訟者，鞭而遣之。

translations.literal: When people came with lawsuits he whipped them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: When litigants came he whipped them and sent them away.

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 籍又甚工草書，筆勢遒放，蓋孔琳之流亞也。

translations.literal: Ji was also very skilled at cursive script; his brush momentum was forceful and free, nearly of Kong Lin's stream.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was also masterful at cursive script; his brush was forceful and free, nearly of Kong Lin's school.

sentences.zh: 湘東王集其文為十卷云。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong collected his writings into ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong collected his writings in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 瞻字思範，弘從孫也。

translations.literal: Zhan, styled Sifan, was Hong's younger brother's son's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan, courtesy name Sifan, was Hong's grand-nephew.

sentences.zh: 祖柳字休季，位光祿大夫、東亭侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liu, styled Xiuji, held the posts of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis of Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu, courtesy name Xiuji, served as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis of Dongting.

sentences.zh: 父猷字世倫，位侍中、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father You, styled Shilun, held the posts of Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His father You, courtesy name Shilun, served as Palace Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 瞻年六歲從師，時有伎經門過，同業皆出觀，瞻獨不視，習業如初。

translations.literal: At six Zhan followed a teacher; once when acrobats passed the gate all his fellows went out to watch, but Zhan alone did not look and studied as before.
translations.idiomatic: At six he followed a teacher; when acrobats passed the gate his classmates all ran out to watch, but Zhan alone kept studying.

sentences.zh: 從父僧達聞而異之，謂其父猷曰：「大宗不衰，寄之此子。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother Sengda heard and was struck; he told Zhan's father You: "The great lineage will not decline—hope rests in this boy.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Sengda heard and marveled; he told Zhan's father You: "The great lineage will not fail—hope rests in this boy.

sentences.zh: 」年十二居父憂，以孝聞。

translations.literal: " At twelve he mourned his father and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: " At twelve he mourned his father and won fame for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 服闋，襲封東亭侯。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he inherited the enfeoffment as Marquis of Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he inherited the marquisate of Dongting.

sentences.zh: 後頗好逸遊，為閭里患，以輕薄稱。

translations.literal: Later he quite loved idle roaming and was a neighborhood nuisance, known for lightness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he took to idle roaming and became a neighborhood nuisance, known for frivolity.

sentences.zh: 及長，折節修士操，涉獵書記，善碁工射。

translations.literal: When grown he restrained himself and cultivated the conduct of a gentleman, broadly read records and documents, and was skilled at chess and archery.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he checked himself and cultivated a gentleman's conduct, read widely, and excelled at chess and archery.

sentences.zh: 歷位驃騎將軍王晏長史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as chief clerk to the Cavalry General Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as chief clerk to the Cavalry General Wang Yan.

sentences.zh: 晏誅，出為晉陵太守。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed he went out as Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was executed he was sent out as Administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 潔己為政，妻子不免饑寒，時號廉平。

translations.literal: He kept himself clean in governance; wife and children did not escape hunger and cold; men of the time called him incorrupt and fair.
translations.idiomatic: He governed cleanly; wife and children still knew hunger and cold; men called him incorrupt and fair.

sentences.zh: 王敬則作亂，瞻赴都，敬則經晉陵郡，人多附之。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Zhan went to the capital; Jingze passed through Jinling commandery and many people attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze rebelled, Zhan went to the capital; Jingze passed through Jinling and many people joined him.

sentences.zh: 敬則敗，台軍討賊黨，瞻言愚人易動，不足窮法。

translations.literal: When Jingze was defeated, court troops punished the rebel partisans; Zhan said foolish men are easily moved and need not be pursued to the full law.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingze was defeated, court troops punished the rebels; Zhan argued that fools are easily swayed and need not be pursued to the full penalty.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Qi agreed.

sentences.zh: 所全萬數。

translations.literal: Those he spared numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Those he spared numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，為侍中、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Liang platform was established he became Palace Attendant and Director of the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang regime was founded he became Palace Attendant and Director of the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 性率亮，居選部，所舉多行其意。

translations.literal: By nature he was frank and bright; in the Selection Office his recommendations mostly followed his own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Frank and open by nature, in the Selection Office he mostly promoted men as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 頗嗜酒，每飲或彌日，而精神朗贍，不廢簿領。

translations.literal: He quite loved wine; whenever he drank it might last a whole day, yet his spirit was clear and ample and he did not neglect documents.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine; a bout might last all day, yet his mind stayed clear and he never neglected paperwork.

sentences.zh: 梁武每稱瞻有三術：射、棋、酒也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang often said Zhan had three arts: archery, chess, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang often said Zhan had three arts: archery, chess, and wine.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡康侯。

translations.literal: When he died his posthumous title was Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously titled Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 子長玄早卒。

translations.literal: His son Changxuan died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changxuan died young.

sentences.zh: 弘四弟：虞、柳、孺、曇首。

translations.literal: Hong's four younger brothers: Yu, Liu, Ru, and Tanshou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had four younger brothers: Yu, Liu, Ru, and Tanshou.

sentences.zh: 虞字休仲，位廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Xiuzhong, held the post of Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, courtesy name Xiuzhong, served as Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 虞子深字景度，有美名，位新安太守。

translations.literal: Yu's son Shen, styled Jingdu, had a fine name and held the post of Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Shen, courtesy name Jingdu, enjoyed a fine reputation and served as Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 柳、孺事列於前，曇首別卷。

translations.literal: Liu and Ru are treated earlier; Tanshou has a separate scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Liu and Ru are treated earlier; Tanshou has a separate scroll.

sentences.zh: 玄孫 沖

translations.literal: Great-grandson Chong
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandson Chong

sentences.zh: 沖字長深，弘玄孫也。

translations.literal: Chong, styled Changshen, was Hong's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Chong, courtesy name Changshen, was Hong's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 祖僧衍，位侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengyan held the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengyan served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父茂璋字胤光，仕梁位給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Maozhang, styled Yinguang, served Liang as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maozhang, courtesy name Yinguang, served Liang as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安公主，卒于齊世。

translations.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an, younger sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in the Qi era.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an, Emperor Wu of Liang's sister; she had died in the Qi era.

sentences.zh: 武帝深鍾愛沖，賜爵東安亭侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply cherished Chong and bestowed on him the rank Marquis of Dong'an Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished Chong deeply and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Dong'an Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中，南郡太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Palace Attendant and Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Palace Attendant and Administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 習于法令，政號平理，雖無赫赫之譽，久而見思。

translations.literal: Practiced in statutes, his governance was called fair and orderly; though without loud fame, over time men remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in law, he governed fairly; though he won no loud fame, men remembered him in time.

sentences.zh: 曉音樂，習歌舞，善與人交，貴遊之中，聲名籍甚。

translations.literal: He understood music, practiced song and dance, and was good at friendship; among the noble wanderers his name and reputation were very great.
translations.idiomatic: He knew music, song, and dance, and made friends easily; among the gilded youth his fame was great.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，元帝承制，沖求解南郡讓王僧辯，並獻女伎十人，以助軍賞。

translations.literal: In the chaos of Hou Jing, Emperor Yuan by provisional order had Chong ask to be relieved of Nan commandery for Wang Sengbian and present ten female performers to aid military reward.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion, Emperor Yuan provisionally had Chong surrender Nan commandery to Wang Sengbian and offer ten female performers as military reward.

sentences.zh: 侯景平，授丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified he was appointed Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was suppressed he was appointed Intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 魏平江陵，敬帝為太宰承制，以沖為左長史。

translations.literal: When Wei pacified Jiangling, Emperor Jing as Grand Preceptor by provisional order made Chong Left Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Jiangling, Emperor Jing as Grand Preceptor provisionally made Chong Left Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 紹泰中，累遷左光祿大夫、尚書左僕射、開府儀同三司，給扶。

translations.literal: In the Shaotai era he was promoted in succession to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Left Masters of Writing, and Grand Preceptor with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, granted a staff for support.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shaotai era he rose to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Vice Director of the Left Masters of Writing, and Grand Preceptor Equal to the Three Excellencies with a support staff.

sentences.zh: 沖有子三十人，並致通官；

translations.literal: Chong had thirty sons, all reaching prominent office;
translations.idiomatic: Chong had thirty sons, all of whom reached prominent office;

sentences.zh: 第十二子瑒。

translations.literal: the twelfth son Yang.
translations.idiomatic: the twelfth son Yang.

sentences.zh: 沖第十二子 瑒

translations.literal: Chong's twelfth son Yang
translations.idiomatic: Chong's twelfth son Yang

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，曆中書令，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne he served in succession as Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Office of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne Yang served in succession as Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Office of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 瑒性寬和，務清靜，無所抑揚。

translations.literal: Yang's nature was mild and harmonious; he pursued clarity and quiet and had nothing to suppress or elevate.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was mild and harmonious, seeking clarity and quiet, pressing nothing up or down.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加侍中，參選事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Left Masters of Writing, added as Palace Attendant, and shared in appointment affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Director of the Left Masters of Writing and Palace Attendant, sharing in appointments.

sentences.zh: 瑒居家篤睦，每歲時饋遺，遍及近親。

translations.literal: At home Yang was deeply harmonious; each year at the seasons he sent gifts reaching all near kin.
translations.idiomatic: At home Yang was deeply harmonious; each season he sent gifts to all near kin.

sentences.zh: 敦誘諸弟，稟其規訓。

translations.literal: He earnestly instructed his younger brothers and they received his rules and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly taught his younger brothers, who followed his instruction.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈特進，諡曰光子。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously given Special Grand Master; his posthumous title was Duke Guangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Special Grand Master with the title Duke Guangzi.

sentences.zh: 瑒弟 瑜

translations.literal: Yang's younger brother Yu
translations.idiomatic: Yang's younger brother Yu

sentences.zh: 論曰：語云：「不有君子，其能國乎？

translations.literal: Commentary says: The saying goes: "Without gentlemen, how can there be a state?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The saying runs: "Without gentlemen, how can there be a state?

sentences.zh: 晉自中原沸騰，介居江左，以一隅之地，抗衡上國，年移三百，蓋有憑焉。

translations.literal: From the time Jin's central plains seethed and they dwelt east of the river, with one corner of land balancing the upper state, years moved three hundred—surely there was reliance.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Jin's heartland boiled and they held east of the river, one corner balancing the northern empire for three hundred years—they surely had something to lean on.

sentences.zh: 其初諺云：「王與馬，共天下。

translations.literal: At the beginning the proverb said: "Wang and Ma share all under heaven together.
translations.idiomatic: An early proverb said: "The Wangs and the Mas share the realm.

sentences.zh: 」蓋王氏人倫之盛，實始是矣。

translations.literal: " Truly the Wang clan's human excellence began here.
translations.idiomatic: " The Wang clan's eminence among men truly began here.

sentences.zh: 及夫休元弟兄，並舉棟樑之任，下逮世嗣，無虧文雅之風。

translations.literal: When Xiuyuan and his brothers together bore pillar-and-beam responsibility, down to later heirs, the refined literary wind was not lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuyuan and his brothers together bore the weight of state, down through later heirs the refined literary tradition did not fail.

sentences.zh: 其所以簪纓不替，豈徒然也。

translations.literal: That their official caps were not replaced—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: That their line held rank without break—was it mere chance?

sentences.zh: 僧達倡狂成性，元長躁競不止。

translations.literal: Sengda's wild arrogance was his nature; Yuanchang's restless striving never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Sengda was wild arrogance incarnate; Yuanchang's restless ambition never ceased.
